deep.reconstruction:
This page is a short outline headed 'Convergenz der Reihen'. It has nothing directly to do with the zeta-function and saddle-point computations on the neighbouring folios. It reads like notes for an elementary lecture on infinite series.

(1) Definition. For the infinite series a_0 + a_1 + a_2 + ... the partial sums are s_n = a_0 + ... + a_n. If lim_{n->oo} s_n = C exists, the series is called convergent and C is its sum. Riemann first wrote 'so nennt man C die Summe' and struck it out, then reordered the sentence: 'so nennt man die Reihe convergent, und C die Summe der unendlichen Reihe'.

(2) Necessary conditions. Convergence requires lim (s_{n+1} - s_n) = 0, i.e. lim a_n = 0. More generally it requires s_{n+m} - s_n = a_{n+1} + ... + a_{n+m} -> 0. In his words, this block is 'beliebig klein, wenn n nur hinreichend groß genommen wird' (arbitrarily small once n is large enough). This is the Cauchy criterion, stated here as a necessary condition. The top of the page shows the identity s_{n+m} - s_n = a_{n+1} + ... + a_{n+m} that underlies it.

(3) Positive series and the harmonic counterexample. He considers series p_0 + p_1 + p_2 + ... with all terms positive and finally decreasing to zero ('welche zuletzt ins Unendliche abnehmen'). He shows that lim a_n = 0 alone is not sufficient, using 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + ... and the estimate 1/(n+1) + ... + 1/(2n) > 1/2.
- Implicit step (mine): each of the n terms is at least 1/(2n), so the block is at least n/(2n) = 1/2.
- Hence s_{2n} - s_n does not tend to 0, the Cauchy condition fails, and the harmonic series diverges although its terms tend to 0.

(4) Unfinished remainder. A struck 'Entweder' is followed by 'Wenn die Summe der Reihe convergirt', the symbol s_n, and a small sketch, apparently a number line with 0, n and A marked. The page ends with C - s_n above a horizontal rule. This is evidently the start of a discussion of the remainder (or of the monotone partial sums of a positive series approaching a bound). It is not carried out.
errors: The inequality 1/(n+1)+...+1/(2n) > 1/2 is strict only for n >= 2. For n = 1 the block is exactly 1/2, so in general it is >= 1/2. This is harmless for the divergence argument.
The Cauchy condition is stated only as necessary ('nothwendig'). Its sufficiency, which is needed for a full criterion, is not stated on this page. This is incomplete rather than wrong.

results.what: Definition of convergence of an infinite series via limit of partial sums
Necessary conditions a_n -> 0 and a_{n+1}+...+a_{n+m} -> 0 for large n
Divergence of the harmonic series via 1/(n+1)+...+1/(2n) >= 1/2
results.usually_credited_to: Nicole Oresme (c. 1350); the variant also appears with Jakob/Johann Bernoulli

deep.surprise_reason: These are entirely standard textbook or lecture-note basics on convergence of series, well known since Cauchy (and Oresme for the harmonic series). They add nothing non-standard. At most the page documents Riemann preparing elementary teaching material.

checkable.asserts: For n=1 the block equals exactly 1/2 (non-strict case).

transcription_corrections: The heading is 'Convergenz der Reihen.'; the transcription is correct.
In 'Damit eine Reihe convergirt...' the condition is 'lim (s_{n+1}-s_n) = 0', and the following clause should read 'aber auch lim(s_{n+m}-s_n)=0, also a_{n+1}+a_{n+2}+...+a_{n+m} beliebig klein'.
The last term in the positive series line is p_n, written slightly unclearly as 'p_{n}' at the end of the line.
The final sketch '0 o n - A' is better read as a number-line diagram (points 0, n, A) than as a formula.
In the inequality line the denominator 1/(2n) appears to have a struck correction in the manuscript.
